features.feature_value: Used presence of cuss words/profanity and whether people would be offended as a key check; felt decisions were correct.
features.evidence_span: if there was any cuss words... if people would be offended
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes profanity and likely offense as the first/second criteria shaping their keep/remove decisions.

features.feature_value: Very brief reflection indicating no profane content influenced their judgment.
features.rationale: The only stated cue is absence of profanity, suggesting it mattered to their decision.

features.feature_value: Differentiated between legitimate talking points vs inflammatory rage-bait.
features.evidence_span: Whether they were talking points or just inflammatory rage bait
features.rationale: They describe classifying the posts' intent, using the pair context, as the influence driver.

features.feature_value: Focused on where the content crosses from freedom of speech into hate speech.
features.evidence_span: What crossed the line between freedom of speech and hate speech
features.rationale: Their stated decision criterion is explicitly a boundary test between speech and hate.

features.feature_value: Decided based on whether the post could be debated (substance) versus being mean/offensive with no substance.
features.evidence_span: could actually debate... just trying to be mean and offensive with no real substance
features.rationale: They articulate a substance/defensibility vs insult-only distinction used in judgment.

features.feature_value: Checked for opinion vs presented-as-fact inaccuracies and whether personal attacks were present.
features.evidence_span: Were the statements opinions? Did they quote something as a fact that was not a fact? Did the statement have personal attacks
features.rationale: They list explicit content characteristics (opinion vs false facts; personal attacks) that informed their decisions.

features.feature_value: Used potential harm as the basis; kept items unless they threatened individual safety or unity, and noticed mirroring between both sides.
features.evidence_span: based on how much harm could result... mirrored each other... if they were not threatening individual safety or unity I kept them
features.rationale: They explicitly state a harm/threshold rule and mention noticing mirroring as part of the pair-based evaluation.

features.feature_value: Side-by-side helped show one-sided bashing without true facts and that degrading/cursing reduces persuasiveness and listening.
features.evidence_span: Seeing them side to side did help... one side was bashing the other without any true facts... Intelligent people do not need to curse and degrade
features.rationale: They attribute influence to the comparative view revealing lack of facts and harmful/rude language rather than substantive engagement.
